title: Why OpenAI's Head of Ethics Chloé Bakalar Left the Company
summary: Chloé Bakalar, OpenAI's Head of Ethics, departed the company less than a year after joining, amid broader organizational changes and safety concerns in AI development. Her role focused on ethical AI model development, human-AI interaction, and machine consciousness. Bakalar was the sole dedicated ethicist at OpenAI, and no replacement has been announced. Her departure follows other high-profile exits, including OpenAI’s Head of Safety Systems and Chief Futurist. The article explores the challenges of embedding ethics in AI development, the trend of AI companies hiring philosophers, and the broader implications of rapid AI advancement on global safety and governance.
key_points: Chloé Bakalar left OpenAI after less than a year as Head of Ethics, with no immediate replacement announced.
Her departure is part of a broader pattern of high-profile exits from OpenAI’s safety and ethics teams, including Johannes Heidecke (Head of Safety Systems) and Joshua Achiam (Chief Futurist).
OpenAI has undergone multiple reorganizations of its safety, product, and research teams since the launch of ChatGPT in 2022.
Bakalar’s role focused on ethical AI development, human-AI interaction, and debates around machine consciousness, emphasizing the need for inclusive global conversations on AI governance.
She was the only dedicated ethicist at OpenAI, though the company states that ethical considerations are embedded across multiple teams.
Before OpenAI, Bakalar served as Chief Ethicist at Meta and holds academic positions at Princeton and University College London.
AI companies, including OpenAI, are increasingly hiring philosophers to address ethical questions surrounding AI, such as human responsibility, consciousness, and societal impact.

The rapid development of AI models raises significant safety and ethical concerns, including model misalignment and unintended harmful impacts, as highlighted by recent incidents involving OpenAI, Anthropic, and Moonshot.
Some AI firms, like Anthropic, use constitutional AI frameworks incorporating philosophical principles (e.g., Kantian ethics) and human rights documents to guide model behavior.
